newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - August 6.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on August 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesia said it will buy 12 Russian Sukhoi Su-30 jet fighters and eight MI-17 military helicopters after it rejected an offer of nine F-16 aircraft from the United States two months ago because of persistent criticism of its human rights record in the U.S. Congress.
Satellite imagery has found more than 600 "hot spots" where burning off or clearly has taken place on the large islands of Sumatra and Kalimantan since March.
President Suharto has given Information Minister Hartono the green light to join the Association of Indonesian Moslem Intellectuals (ICMI).

President Suharto has questioned South African President Nelson Mandela's letter which called on Jakarta to release jailed East Timorese rebel leader Xanana Gusmao. He asked whether there were sufficient legal, political and moral reasons to do so.
The Body for the Assessment and Application of Technology (BPPT) and Department of Public Works are preparing to make artificial rain in September to lessen the affects of the dry season.

Three people have been arrested after they took part in the burning down of a police station in the coastal resort town of Pelabuhan Ratu at the weekend when an angry crowd attacked police because they were disastified with the speed of the investigation of the murder of a local teacher in May.
